body:
## Module 4 in two minutes

Every other AI output in this curriculum passes through a human before it reaches anyone who matters. **Yours goes straight to the employee** — unmediated, at scale, about their own money and their own health, in the company's voice. They don't experience it as a model's output. They experience it as what the company told them, and they act on it.

And it doesn't only send. **It receives**, which nothing else in this curriculum does.

Start with the metric, because your vendor will lead with the wrong one. **Deflection counts an abandoned conversation and a confidently wrong answer exactly the same as a genuine fix** — all three look like "didn't come back." Measure instead: repeat contact, escalation appropriateness, **answer correctness against the governing document**, and voluntary return. Only the third catches a fluent wrong answer the employee accepted.

And hold onto the structural version: **an employee who got a wrong answer and acted on it never appears in any of your metrics.** They didn't come back, they didn't complain. They're a satisfied number in your deflection rate and a live problem in your organization.

### The model isn't the variable. Your documents are.

A capable model reading a superseded summary plan description produces a fluent, well-structured, confidently wrong answer. A weaker model reading a current document produces a correct one. **Model quality shows up in tone and edge cases. Document-set quality shows up in whether the answer is true.**

Which reframes the failure: **an answer drawn from a superseded document is not a bad summary. It is a misstatement made by the employer** — in writing, to an employee, about their own money or health. Nothing was hallucinated. Your corpus was wrong and the model repeated it faithfully.

Three controls, cheapest first. **One source per topic, with the others removed from the index** — not marked superseded, removed, because retrieval respects what is reachable rather than what you intended. **An effective-date field on every retrievable document, and a rule that the capability may not answer from one without it** — the best standing control here, because it converts an invisible failure into a refusal. And **a named owner per topic**, which fails the same way it does in Module 1 when assigned to a team.

And the sequencing: this isn't AI work, it's the prerequisite for the AI work — and it's the first thing cut when a launch date moves. **If the corpus isn't ready for a topic, narrow the scope rather than launching broadly.**

**The full module's sharpest content is the notice problem, and it carries a counsel gate.** Employment counsel identify that an employer **may** receive sufficient notice of an FMLA-qualifying condition, or of an ADA accommodation request, *through a chatbot interaction* — with interference or denial-of-rights exposure where the bot responds inappropriately. And an employee volunteering health details **may** create obligations to protect that communication as confidential medical information. Every one of those is *may*: risk analysis from the people who defend these claims, not a holding, and no controlling decision was found. That is why the gate is real.

The operational consequence doesn't wait for the law to resolve: **notice to the bot is notice to you.** Escalation routing is a legal control, not a design preference.

And the hard part — **people do not use the words.** *"I'm struggling to get in for 9am since my treatment started"* is an accommodation request containing neither the word accommodation nor disability. So keyword routing fails in the direction that hurts. Route on **topic proximity and uncertainty**, accept a false-positive rate a product manager will dislike (over-routing costs a coordinator's time; under-routing costs a statutory obligation nobody noticed), and never let the capability close the loop on something it just routed.

Then three more on the same surface: consistency is now **logged and cuts both ways**; AI disclosure at first contact has been enforceable since **2 August 2026**; and **always keep a human route, never harder to find than the bot.**
